newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CHINESE NEWSPAPERS - AUG 14.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- First in nine-part series, "Change in the East", focusing on economic restructuring in the eastern coastal areas
- The State Commission for Restructuring the Economy and the Propaganda Department host a symposium on economic restructuring.
- A shortage of parking space becomes a serious problem in big cities.
XINHUA DAILY TELEGRAPH
- China's economic restructuring achieves breakthroughs in theory, practice, and method of reform since the Communist Party decided to establish a socialist market economy in 1992.
- Premier Li Peng tells Cambodian acting head of state Chea Sim that internal problems of Cambodia should be solved by the Cambodian people on their own.
- Multi-party cooperation under leadership of the Chinese Communist Party has improved since 1992 due to efforts by the Communist Party Central Committee.
- China's poverty alleviation programmes have improved rapidly, with some 12 million people expected to rise above the poverty line this year.
SHENZHEN SPECIAL ZONE DAILY
- Shenzhen airport closes for two hours due to interference from paging stations.
MARKET DAILY
- Losses in the wool-spinning industry reach 430 million yuan in 1996.
- China's household savings reach 385.208 billion yuan by end-1996.
CHINA SECURITIES
- Wuxi Little Swan Co sets up technical development centre in the United States.
- Five Chinese transportation, post, and telecommunications enterprises list overseas in the first half of this year, raising 11.023 billion yuan of capital.
HEALTH DAILY
- People's Insurance Company of China's life insurance premium income rises 107.5 percent to 18.14 billion yuan in first half of 1997.
INTERNATIONAL ECONOMIC DAILY
- State General Administration of Taxation issues urgent circular on giving priority to textile firms for reimbursement of export tax credits.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- China's commercial housing stock reaches 66.243 million square metres by the end of 1996.
LIBERATION DAILY
- Jiangsu province exports 1.3 tonnes of sugar to Yemen.
CHINA DAILY
- State Education Commission sets rules for non-government run schools.
- China will broadcast a documentary on the Dalai Lama.
- Trade officials say major retailers are embroiled in a price-cutting campaign to promote sales.
- People's Insurance Company of China provides $78.9 million in export credit insurance for the export of five ships to Iran
- State Development Bank of China loans 700 million yuan to Harbin Power Equipment Co for providing equipment to the Three Gorges dam project.
